To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the drivers of SME high social performance (HSP) are the internal drivers of a positive organizational culture and a strong commitment to social issues, as well as the external drivers of a positive external environment.
the social performance of small and medium enterprises (SMes) is determined by the interplay of drivers and barriers to their social performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a specific type of social issue: social exclusion.
understanding the role that social performance (SP) plays in the context of SMEs.
understanding the role and importance of social issues in small and medium enterprises (hereafter referred to as SMEs), and the drivers and barriers that influence their management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social performance of SMEs is not as good as it could be, but it is improving.
the social performance of SMEs is not only determined by internal and external drivers but is also influenced by the interplay between these drivers.
the social performance of SMEs is not a simple matter of good or bad, but a complex interplay of drivers and barriers, which are often related to the key stakeholder groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the role of social issues and social issues management for SMEs.
we have identified a four‐cell model of SME SIM responses based on the key drivers and barriers that SMEs face in addressing social issues.
we have developed a theoretical framework for SME social performance that integrates internal and external drivers as well as barriers to SP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a better understanding of the drivers and barriers of high social performance of SMEs and the implications for theory and practice.
the social performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) can vary widely depending on the type of social issue they face.
SMEs are more likely to engage with social issues when there is a high level of social awareness and when the business environment provides a supportive environment for social issues management.
